commits.message:
[EASI-5064] Bump Go to 1.27.3 and Node to 24.22.1 (eMudhra CA compromise) (#3578)

* [EASI-5064] Bump Go to 1.27.3 and Node to 24.22.1

Picks up the patched trust stores for the eMudhra intermediate CA
compromise (https://we-have-a-problem.com). Node 20 is end-of-life and
has no patched release, so this moves to Node 24 (matching MINT).
Rebuilding also pulls a fresh gcr.io/distroless/base with the patched
Debian ca-certificates.

* [EASI-5064] Upgrade ca-certificates explicitly in the Go base stage

The final distroless image copies its CA bundle from the golang base
stage, not from distroless. Upgrade ca-certificates there before
update-ca-certificates so trust store fixes don't depend on how fresh
the golang image tag is, and our custom CAs are layered on top.

* [EASI-5064] Move Cypress image to Node 24 with patched trust store

The final Cypress stage was still cypress/base:20.14.0. cypress/base has
no 24.22.1 tag yet, and 24.22.0's bundled CA store still trusts the
compromised eMudhra intermediates, so upgrade Debian's patched
ca-certificates and run yarn install with --use-openssl-ca.

* [EASI-5064] Use node:24.22.0 images with patched trust store until 24.22.1 is published

The node:24.22.1 Docker Hub tags exist but have no platform images yet,
so image builds fail with 'no match for platform in manifest'. Use
24.22.0 for now; its bundled CA store still trusts the compromised
eMudhra intermediates, so upgrade the distro's patched ca-certificates
and run yarn with --use-openssl-ca. .nvmrc and CI (setup-node, which
installs from nodejs.org) stay on 24.22.1.

* [EASI-5064] Bump golang.org/x/tools to v0.52.0 for Go 1.27.3

gqlgen code generation (go generate) exits 1 with no output under Go
1.27.3 with x/tools v0.44.0, deleting generated.go and models_gen.go.
Main fails the same way on 1.27.3 and works on 1.27.1. Upgrading x/tools
(and its x/net, x/sync, x/sys, x/text deps) fixes it; regenerated code is
byte-for-byte identical. MINT already uses x/tools v0.51.0.
commits.author: Peyton T

commits.message:
[MINT-3935] Bump Go to 1.27.3 and Node to 24.22.1 (eMudhra CA compromise) (#2615)

* [MINT-3935] Bump Go to 1.27.3 and Node to 24.22.1

Picks up the patched trust stores for the eMudhra intermediate CA
compromise (https://we-have-a-problem.com). Rebuilding also pulls a
fresh gcr.io/distroless/base with the patched Debian ca-certificates.

* [MINT-3935] Upgrade ca-certificates explicitly in the Go base stage

The final distroless image copies its CA bundle from the golang base
stage, not from distroless. Upgrade ca-certificates there before
update-ca-certificates so trust store fixes don't depend on how fresh
the golang image tag is, and our custom CAs are layered on top.

* [MINT-3935] Use node:24.22.0 images with patched trust store until 24.22.1 is published

The node:24.22.1 Docker Hub tags exist but have no platform images yet,
so image builds fail with 'no match for platform in manifest'. Use
24.22.0 for now; its bundled CA store still trusts the compromised
eMudhra intermediates, so upgrade the distro's patched ca-certificates
and run yarn with --use-openssl-ca. .nvmrc and CI (setup-node, which
installs from nodejs.org) stay on 24.22.1.

commits.message:
fix(backend): build with Go 1.27.3 for the crypto/x509 revocation fix (#619)

The post-merge Snyk scan on main now fails on Go 1.25.14. It reports a
high-severity certificate-revocation issue in `crypto/x509`
(SNYK-GOLANG-STDCRYPTOX509-21400137 / GO-2026-6809), which is fixed in
Go 1.26.10 and 1.27.3. Because that scan gates the deploy jobs, the run
for #617 skipped every DEV and PROD job, and every later merge to main
will do the same until the backend moves. This moves the backend to Go
1.27.3.

## Changes

- `backend/go.mod`: `go 1.25.14` → `go 1.27.3`. `go mod tidy` leaves
`go.sum` unchanged.
- `backend/Dockerfile`: builder image `golang:1.25.14-bookworm` →
`golang:1.27.3-bookworm`.
- `.github/workflows/analysis.yml` (lint go): Go pin `1.27.1` → `1.27.3`
and staticcheck `v0.8.1` → `v0.8.2`. setup-go sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`,
so a lint pin below the go.mod version would refuse to build. v0.8.2 is
the first staticcheck release that reads Go 1.27.2+ export data, the
failure #611 worked around. The comment there is updated to match.

The other workflows read the version from `go-version-file:
backend/go.mod` and pick up the change on their own.

Merging this also deploys #617's dev CloudFront change, which is on main
but was never applied.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` on Go 1.27.3
- [x] staticcheck v0.8.2 clean
- [x] `go test -short ./...` and `go test -short -race ./...`
- [x] `make test-integration` (builds the API image from the updated
Dockerfile)
- [x] `make test-e2e` (Emberfall, 0 failed)
- [x] `make generate-openapi` produces no diff
- [x] govulncheck no longer reports GO-2026-6809
- [ ] Analysis `snyk test` and `lint go` pass on this PR
- [ ] Post-merge orchestration run reaches DEV and PROD

govulncheck still reports reachable advisories in
`github.com/xuri/excelize/v2` (GO-2026-6688, GO-2026-6684) and
`golang.org/x/text` (GO-2026-6629, GO-2026-5970). Those are module
upgrades, separate from the toolchain, and are not part of this PR.

commits.message:
feat(misc#379): require TLS 1.3 at the dev CloudFront edge (#617)

Part of CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#379 (dev only; the impl and prod PR
closes it)

### What and why

This sets the dev CloudFront distribution's viewer security policy to
`TLSv1.3_2025`, which refuses TLS 1.2. CloudFront offers hybrid
post-quantum key exchange only under TLS 1.3, so this closes the
classical path at the edge.

The setting is now a variable, `cloudfront_minimum_protocol_version`,
whose default is the current `TLSv1.2_2021`. Only `dev.tfvars` sets the
new value, so impl and prod plan no change. The ticket holds dev for at
least a week before impl and prod, and a follow-up PR sets those.

### Why it is safe to turn off TLS 1.2

The first 14 days of CloudFront logs are in
[ztmf-misc#379](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/379).
TLS 1.2 was 0.11% of prod HTTPS requests (33 of 31,211) and 0.14% in
dev, and none of it came from people using ZTMF. Most of it was
Microsoft's link scanners and preview bots. ZTMF has no login canary,
and no CMS monitoring or scanner showed up on TLS 1.2.

### Visible change

In dev, a client that can only do TLS 1.2 gets a handshake failure.
Browsers and other TLS 1.3 clients see no change. Plain HTTP requests
still get their redirect.

### Testing

`terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass. `make test-unit`
passes; no Go code changed. After the dev deploy I will run the probe
from the ticket against `dev.ztmf.cms.gov`: a TLS 1.2 only client should
be refused, and a TLS 1.3 client should negotiate X25519MLKEM768.
